statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows where we will land, and none of us can even guess the odds. Whatever we choose holds for a generation. I can't bet my household on being in the top fifth, and I don't think any of you can either. So I am asking one question: if I turn out to be at the bottom, which plan leaves me best off? Hazel does. It gives the lowest group 41 thousand, which is nearly double today's figure and the highest that can be sustained. Birch and Alder also protect the bottom well, and I rank them next. Cedar has the highest average, but it pushes the poorest down to 15 thousand without health coverage. That is a gamble each of us might lose, with no second convention to fix it. I rank Hazel first, and I'm willing to talk about Birch or Alder if that is how we reach nine votes.
